codeReview.summary: The ordering and clip work appears aligned with VAL-SCENE-001 through VAL-SCENE-005, but the submitted commit also changes replay validation and that new logic still accepts some unbalanced scoped-layer subranges, so the feature bundle is not safe to accept as-is.

issues.description: `validateReplayRange` only inspects the selected `paintRecords[range]` slice and never computes the scoped-layer depth at the range boundaries. For a range like `1..<2` over `startLayer, primitive, endLayer`, the loop sees only `.primitive`, returns balanced, and `replay` succeeds even though the range begins and ends inside an unmatched scoped layer. That violates the safe-failure requirement for ranges that start or end inside unmatched markers.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The feature metadata and handoff scope this work to VAL-SCENE-001 through VAL-SCENE-005, but the shipped commit also includes bridge/replay files outside that feature surface. The mission guidance documents validation and architecture, but it does not explicitly require workers to isolate unrelated working-tree changes before committing feature work.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Feature metadata for `scene-family-ordering-and-batching` fulfills only VAL-SCENE-001..005; the handoff summary only describes `GPUIScene.swift` and `GPUISceneTests.swift`; `git show --stat ddddac2772eb4ff44d849a229e811a7746f3eef9` also includes `Sources/SwiftWindowsGraphics/GPUISceneBridge.swift` and `Tests/SwiftWindowsCoreLogicTests/GPUISceneBridgeTests.swift`.
